I couldn't finish [i]Red Trigger[/i].

Not only is it [i]not[/i] about communism, it's not about anything. It's a super simple, super derivative puzzle game that manages to be a totally horrendous experience due to major issues with graphical fidelity and overall design. [i]Red Trigger[/i]'s most obvious influence is [i]Portal[/i], from which developer Maxime Vézina seems to have taken a liking to sterile white corridors as a form of minimalistic art direction, which would be fine if the way 'white corridors' had been accomplished weren't simply solid blocks of untextured white. Half the time it's impossible to comprehend where a platform ends and the next begins, because literally everything is just solid colours. I played less than an hour, and somehow [i]Red Trigger[/i] still almost made me throw up on several occasions as my crosshair was lost in the sea of blinding white that is the environment. It's the kind of game where you get vertigo from looking at the intersect between two walls. There is no point of reference for any of your camera or character movement, so already the whole premise of this being a puzzle/platformer has gone out the window.

The only tool you're given is a Google Sketchup gun which you can use to extend out platforms coloured red to create walkways or propel yourself across chasms, sort of like a simplified version of the mechanics from the similarly derivative [i]Q.U.B.E[/i], a game which at the very least had textures. The thing that really stops [i]Red Trigger[/i] from finding it's feet is just how purely unoriginal it is. There isn't even an [i]attempt[/i] to hook players in, you just launch it up, walk forward and gameplay starts. The entire game can be summarised by brief comparisons to other, better games. Unlikely many bad games, [i]Red Trigger[/i] fails to even be truly bad - it's just bland. Had it contained at least one original mechanic or exciting gameplay feature it may have at least held [i]some[/i] value. As it stands, the game may be somewhat tolerable to those new to gaming as a medium, but there generally isn't much in it for anyone who's played a puzzle game in the last 15 years.

Red Trigger is an ok puzzle game, but with a few problems.
1.The entire premise of creating pillars isn't that interesting. It leads to some boring puzzles that invlove more observation than contemplation. This means that you will die to a puzzle after figuring out the solution strictly because you didn't duck under a far away moving wall you didn't know to duck under. Or because you couldn't see a pillar you had to activate until the second attempt.
2.Deaths feel cheap and unnecessary. The games deaths are normally because of the aforementioned purely observational puzzles. It is not "well I messed up that." it is "Why was that necessary to the puzzle?".
3.The game has a toggle crouch and a minimalist style. I don't know about you, but those two things do not match well for me if there is no indicator. Since some puzzles require crouching for no apparent reason you will often find yourself crouching and not have noticed it because 99% of the game is pure white walls meaning there's no real change of perspective.
